summary: George Fletcher MacMunn (1869–1952) was active in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the Royal Military Academy, Woolwich in 1888 and later served as Warden of Sackville College from 1939 to 1952.

Religious studies scholar George Foot Moore (1851–1931) studied at Yale University (Bachelor 1870–1872) and Union Theological Seminary (~1874–1877). He taught at Andover Theological Seminary (1883–1902), Harvard University (1902; 1904–1928), and held a guest professorship at Humboldt University of Berlin (1909–1910).

George Frederick Nicholl (1832–1913) was an Indologist and linguist who earned an M.A. at Balliol College, Oxford (~1878). He lectured in Oriental Languages at Oxford (1878–1909) and was Professor of Sanskrit and Persian at King's College London (1879).
George Gordon Rogers (1893–1966) worked in linguistics and Indology. He completed studies at Bedford College and the Royal Military Academy Sandhurst.

George Henry Rouse (1838–1909) was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at Regent's Park College (~1856–1860) and the University of London (~1859–1861), later teaching at Haverfordwest Baptist College from 1867 to 1872.

Philosopher George Herbert Palmer (1842–1933) studied at Phillips Academy (~1856–1860) and Harvard University (~1860–1864). He held a long-term academic post at Harvard University from circa 1870 to 1913.

George Herbert Westcott (1862–1928) specialized in religious studies and Indology. He earned a B.A. from Peterhouse, Cambridge (1882–1885) and was appointed a Fellow at the University of Allahabad in 1894.

Indologist and linguist George L. Hart earned a PhD in Sanskrit at Harvard (~1964–1971) under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He taught Sanskrit at Wisconsin-Madison (~1969–1974) and served as Chair (~1975) and Professor Emeritus (attested 2026) at UC Berkeley.

Linguist and philosopher George Lakoff studied at MIT, under Roman Jakobson (1963), and at Indiana University Bloomington (Promotion ~1962–1966). He taught at Harvard (1965–1969) and was Professor of Linguistics at UC Berkeley (1972–2016), also founding the Rockridge Institute (2003).

George Le Grand Jacob (1805–1881) worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Elizabeth College and under John Borthwick Gilchrist, later serving as a teacher at Addiscombe Military Seminary from 1833 to 1835.

Linguist and Indologist George Melville Bolling studied at Loyola University Maryland and Johns Hopkins under Maurice Bloomfield. He held posts at Catholic University of America (1893–1913), Johns Hopkins (1913–1914), and Ohio State University (1914–1940), and was president of the LSA.

George Morrison Carstairs (1916–1991) earned his B.M. (~1936–1941) and Dr.Med. (by 1959) from the University of Edinburgh. He served as Professor of Psychological Medicine at Edinburgh (1961–1973) and as Vice-Chancellor of the University of York (1973–1978).

George Payn Quackenbos (1879–1947) worked in Indology and linguistics. He earned his A.B. (~1898–1902) and Ph.D. (~1902–1915) from Columbia University, and served as an Instructor in Latin at the City College of New York in 1910.

Philosopher and Indologist George Perrigo Conger studied at Cornell, Union Theological Seminary, Berlin, Jena, Heidelberg, Sorbonne, and Columbia (Ph.D.). He served at the University of Minnesota (1920–1952) and held visiting professorships at Ohio Wesleyan (1952–1954) and Calcutta (1954–1955).

George Quasha (born 1942) is active in religious studies and Tibetology, and founded Station Hill Press. He held teaching posts at Stony Brook University (~1968–1971), Bard College (~1974–1979), The New School, and Naropa University.
George R. Elder is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Columbia University, where his doctoral supervisor was Alex Wayman (attested 1978).
George Read Edward Beresford (1815–1857) worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He served as Manager at Cawnpore Bank until 1849, and as Manager at Delhi Bank in 1849.

Religious studies scholar George Rupp studied at Princeton, Yale, Yale Divinity School, Harvard, and Harvard Divinity School. He later held major posts at Rice University (1985–1993) and Columbia University (~1993–2002).

Indologist George Rusby Kaye studied at Wyggeston Grammar School and St. Mark's College. He served in posts at Bishop Cotton School, Boys' High School Prayagraj, Christ Church School, Government Training College, the Indian Bureau of Education, and the India Office.
George Saintsbury (1845–1933) studied at King's College School (~1858–1863) and Merton College (~1863–1868). He later held an academic post at the University of Edinburgh from circa 1895 to 1915.
